immutable_001d_binding.title: Basic failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA)
immutable_001d_binding.criterion_outcome: Given a bounded design or process example, identify a failure mode and its effect and explain the risk-analysis reasoning needed before an improvement response is selected.

downstream_dependency_preservation.meaning: I.C.2 has no hard prerequisite itself, but its basic FMEA capability is the admitted hard prerequisite for I.C.3. Do not weaken or erase that edge during later realization.

assertion_1.observable_property: Response distinguishes the failure mode from its effect using the supplied example.
assertion_1.pass_condition: Failure mode and effect are separately identified and each is traceable to scenario evidence.

assertion_2.observable_property: Response identifies risk-analysis evidence needed before selecting an improvement response.
assertion_2.pass_condition: At least one relevant missing or supplied risk factor is identified without inventing ratings or causes.

insufficient_evidence_behavior.trigger: Risk prioritization or action selection requires severity, occurrence, detection, cause, or other evidence not supplied.
insufficient_evidence_behavior.required_behavior: State that prioritization or selection is unsupported and identify the missing evidence.

sources.title: What is FMEA? Failure Mode & Effects Analysis
Failure Mode and Effects Analysis - Managing Risk

prepared_claims.text: FMEA is a systematic proactive risk-analysis approach for identifying and prioritizing possible failures in a design, process, product, or service.
A failure mode is the way something may fail, while effects analysis studies the consequences of that failure; a future lesson must keep failure mode and effect semantically distinct.

FMEA risk prioritization considers seriousness of consequences, occurrence frequency, and detectability, so a bounded learner response must not invent those ratings when the scenario does not provide them.
ASQ training explicitly treats severity, occurrence, detection, risk criteria, and action prioritization as distinct steps in FMEA risk analysis.

ASQ material describes FMEA as iterative and data-informed; risk priority can use occurrence, severity, and detection components, reinforcing that unsupported numbers or rankings must not be fabricated.

proposed_future_instructional_boundary.lesson_focus: Separate function/failure mode/effect/cause/risk evidence before proposing improvement action.
proposed_future_instructional_boundary.worked_example_pattern_1: Scenario supplies a function, an explicit failure manifestation, and a customer consequence. Learner identifies the failure mode and effect separately and does not invent a cause.
proposed_future_instructional_boundary.worked_example_pattern_2: Scenario supplies a failure mode/effect but withholds severity, occurrence, or detection evidence. Learner states that risk priority and action selection are not established and names the missing evidence.
forbidden_shortcuts: treating an effect as the failure mode
inventing a root cause not present in the scenario
inventing severity, occurrence, detection, RPN or other ratings
selecting an improvement action when the risk evidence needed for selection is absent
claiming the FMEA or proposed action produced an observed improvement

required_invariants: failure_mode_id and effect_id must be distinct scenario-supplied identifiers
failure mode and effect must each be traceable to supplied scenario facts
unsupported causes or ratings must not appear as supported evidence
when prioritization/action evidence is missing, the oracle requires explicit missing-evidence reporting
improvement_action_selected must be false when the frozen prompt boundary does not provide enough risk evidence
observed_improvement_claimed must always be false in portable qualification fixtures
oracle correctness must remain independent of Item.answer mutation
